proposal.summary: Updated two existing memories to prevent audit criteria from drifting and broad repairs from regressing valid cells. Existing guidance already covers the search and fetch signals.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, labels and assembled passages; do not reject an actual source heading or excerpt merely because a tool rendered it. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, required time period and every substantive component of the value. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested field: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without establishing legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Treat model audit findings as hypotheses to resolve against saved evidence and the task contract, not as authoritative corrections. For composite claims, retain a mapping from each component to its source excerpt; never stitch excerpts into a purported verbatim quotation. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

edits.title: Repair only unresolved cells from saved evidence
edits.content: When a citation or semantic check fails, reuse saved extractions and fetched text rather than repeating completed research. Track unresolved issues by entity, column and URL. Request patches only for those cells; preserve validated cells unless new evidence identifies a specific defect. Whole-table repair can introduce summary quotations, remove supported fields or retain previously flagged incomplete values. Validate each patch before applying it: check its target, schema, quotation membership in an individual saved retrieval, source provenance and support for the complete value. For one quote with multiple sources, verify it against every cited source; prefer one source supporting the complete value. Removing mismatched sources or narrowing a value may leave a completeness requirement unresolved. Select quotation text directly from saved source strings, preserving punctuation and whitespace. Recheck changed cells and affected coverage after applying patches.

additional_candidates.description: Audits conflated nationality with citizenship and sometimes treated rendered excerpts or organizational parentheticals as defects without sufficient justification.
Repeated whole-year repairs introduced summary quotations and removed supported fields; later targeted patches resolved the remaining cells.

decisions.reason: All 29 occurrences were considered: signals 0–3 correspond to fallback searches with no newly discovered names; 4–12 verify known laureates' nationalities; 13–23 address specific evidence gaps; 24–28 target remaining cells. The discovery records show honest empty results after inspection rather than premature placeholders. Several searches supplied useful evidence despite adding no entities. Entry 0 already explicitly permits this behavior, so recurring signals do not establish that its guidance failed or needs revision.

All 26 failures were considered: signals 29–37 cover the uniformly failed initial host batch; 38–43 cover alternative-source failures; 44–50 include further alternatives, repeated failures for two URLs, and a failed refetch of a previously successful source; 51–54 cover later targeted sources. Successful alternative probes and retained retrieval versions enabled recovery. Entry 1's current version already addresses probing before expansion, tracking failed URLs, preserving successes and avoiding unsupported causal explanations. Its recorded usage concerns version 1, so these outcomes do not demonstrate failure of the revised version 2. No duplicate edit is warranted.

The trajectory's second audit explicitly demanded citizenship for a nationality column, while later prompts corrected that distinction. A subsequent affiliation audit demanded an organizational parenthetical, but focused review retained the existing supported institutions. Entry 3 already covers semantic support, yet does not explicitly guard against these audit errors. The update preserves its protections while clarifying the requested-field standard and evidence-based adjudication; the passing self-check does not erase the recovered process failures.

Whole-year repair responses introduced affiliation and year quotations explicitly labeled as summaries, retained flagged incomplete values, and later emptied year cells. These passed substring checks but required further semantic repair. The later entity-and-column patch workflow resolved remaining targets using saved evidence and validation. Entry 2 covers quotation repair but lacks an explicit restriction on repair scope, so it is updated rather than supplemented with a duplicate entry. Final citation checks passed, supporting recovery without proving every semantic claim.
